stem: How did the Three-Fifths Compromise support slavery?

options.label: A
options.text: It established that enslaved people were not equal to free people when determining representation.

options.label: B
options.text: It confirmed that the federal government would be the authority on issues relating to slavery.

options.label: C
options.text: It allowed states to lower their tax rate by adding up the total of all persons living in the state.

options.label: D
options.text: It determined that enslaved people could not be taxed by the states.

visual_elements: Representatives . . . shall be [distributed] among the several States . . . according to their respective Numbers, which shall be determined by adding to the whole Number of free Persons . . . three fifths of all other Persons.  —U.S. Constitution, Article I, Section 2
